call_points.text: About 500 vehicles to be added in FY27; 100-plus already added, remaining 400 by December.
April 2026 volume growth was around 8% YoY.
Lorry hire charges rose 1.73% of revenue, salary 0.74% and vehicle repairs 0.85%; fuel fell 1.77%.
Return on capital employed rose to 25% from 21%; return on equity to 21% from 18%.
Petrochemical and oil-linked commodity demand is softening, which could cap tonnage.
Price hikes are selective and lag diesel moves by about a month.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: During the financial year 2025–26, the assessment for FY 2023–24 was completed under section 143(3) of the Income-tax Act. The assessment was completed by accepting the Return of Income as filed by the Company without any disallowances or any additions. Subsequently, while processing the order, the Centralized Processing Centre (CPC) raised a demand of ₹ 5,186 lakhs under section 156 of IT Act, primarily due to apparent computational errors, including non-grant of credit for advance tax, TDS/ TCS, and tax paid on buyback of shares not being given credit, as well as incorrect levy of interest under section 234B of IT Act. Consequently, the Company has filed a rectification application under section 154 of IT Act. Based on management’s assessment, the erroneous demand made by the Income Tax Department does not represent a valid obligation, as it has arisen solely from processing inaccuracies. Accordingly, no amount is payable by the Company and the likelihood of any cash outflow is considered very remote, and therefore this matter does not give rise to either any potential liability or a contingent liability for the purposes of these financial statements.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Department of Income Tax, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
tax_litigation.status: A Rectification Application has been filed u/s 154 of the Income Act, 1961 on 06.04.2026.

Capex of ₹300-350 Cr in FY27, split ₹100-150 Cr vehicles and ₹200 Cr-plus land and buildings
100-plus net new branches to be opened in FY27

industry: Services > Transport Services > Logistics Solution Provider

operating_notes.text: Realisation per tonne was about ₹8,147 in Q4FY26, up about 3% YoY.
Daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tonnes in Q4FY26; lead distance is 270-280 km and vehicle capacity 15-18 tonnes.
Textile contributes 17-18% of tonnage and agricultural products 10-11%; door-to-door is close to 40% of commodities.

timeline.summary: Dr. Vijay Sankeshwar and Mr. Anand Sankeshwar, promoters, declared no encumbrance on VRL Logistics shares as of March 31, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹852.85 Cr (+5.4% YoY), net profit ₹72.14 Cr.
VRL Logistics reported FY26 total income of ₹3,245 Cr and a 29% jump in PAT to ₹237 Cr, driven by freight rate rationalization and realization improvements.
ANIRUDDHA PHADNAVIS (Chairman) shared the earnings call recording link for Q4FY26 and FY26 results on 19 May 2026.
VRL Logistics' Q4FY26 earnings call guided FY27 tonnage growth at 6-7% and capex at ₹300-350 Cr, after Q4 tonnage turned positive at 3% YoY.
VRL Logistics issued a corrigendum revising its buyback record date to October 22, 2026.
VRL Logistics submitted the letter of offer for its ₹280 Cr buyback at ₹320 per share, scheduled for Oct 27 to Nov 2, 2026.
